subject: Dedicated reservation — staggered onramp, minimum floor & fallback design
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@novaedge.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-16T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated reservation — staggered onramp, minimum floor & fallback design

Jordan,

Thanks for the productive sync this morning. Attached is a concise proposal that maps the capacity ask you outlined to a staging ramp and fallback plan that protects latency while giving you room to optimize spend as usage patterns stabilize. Key summary up front:

- Initial cluster: 24 A100-equivalent GPUs in a 2x12 node pool (min floor 8 GPUs reserved)
- Week 0–6 onramp: soft floor at 8 GPUs, staged activation to 24 GPUs by week 6 based on throughput triggers
- Fallback tiers: automatic regional fallback to EMEA spare pool and model-quantized variant if queue depth > 150 for >5m
- Warm-start credits: 300 pre-warm hours included to cover onboarding surge and profiling windows

Please see the attached PDF (novaedge_reservation_proposal_v2.pdf) and the onramp worksheet for the activation schedule. Main asks from your side so we can finalize:

1) Confirm target 95th percentile latency SLO (you mentioned 120ms for short-chat flows).
2) Flag any procurement dates or PO timing that would require shifting activation windows.
3) Confirm whether model quantization is acceptable as fallback (we included an L2 quantized variant in the plan).

If that looks aligned we can push this to draft terms and lock the reserve lanes.

Best,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com

Attachment: novaedge_reservation_proposal_v2.pdf (PDF, 18 pages)
Attachment: onramp_capacity_worksheet.xlsx (XLSX, 1 sheet)
From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@novaedge.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Katrina Zhou <katrina@novaedge.ai>
Date: 2026-09-17T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation — staggered onramp, minimum floor & fallback design

Marcus —

Appreciate the clear breakdown, this is very helpful. A couple of clarifying notes from our side: 

- 95th p latency target: we can commit to 150ms for initial pilot traffic; will aim for 120ms after optimizations. Please reflect 150ms in the onboarding milestones.
- Procurement: PO window is 4–6 weeks; prefer activation to start in mid-October.
- Quantized fallback: acceptable but need to validate quality on our test prompts. Can the warm-start credits be used for A/B quality runs?

Two quick asks: can you call out the continuous-batching assumptions that drive the 24 GPU peak? We need to show our infra team the queuing model. Also, the minimum floor of 8 GPUs — is that a hard billed minimum or a soft-guarantee with reduced hourly price?

Thanks — will loop Katrina if we need legal to review terms.

—Jordan
Jordan Ellis
Head of Infrastructure, NovaEdge AI
j.ellis@novaedge.ai
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@novaedge.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-18T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation — staggered onramp, minimum floor & fallback design

Jordan —

Quick answers to the two technical asks: 

1) Continuous-batching assumptions: proposal assumes median request length = 32 tokens and 95th sequence length = 256 tokens. With those distributions we benchmarked sustained throughput of ~12 rps per A100-equivalent GPU under the optimized runtime. That is how we derived the 24 GPU peak to sustain your projected QPS with headroom for short-tail bursts. If your observed sequence lengths are longer, the peak scales superlinearly — we can re-run with your telemetry.

2) Minimum floor billing: "soft floor" in our proposal means two parts — reserved capacity that guarantees slots (billed at reserved rate) and a soft warm standby buffer that is billed at a reduced standby rate when unused. The 8 GPU figure is the reserved, billed minimum. We included 300 warm-start hours (no extra bill) to cover ramping profiling and A/B runs; anything beyond that standby buffer is charged at standby rate. We can map this to PO lines explicitly.

Also, warm-start credits can absolutely be applied to dual-run quality comparisons — recommend using them across two 48h windows during week 2 and week 4 for A/B.

If that aligns I'll update the worksheet to annotate per-line billing and add a continuous-batching appendix.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@novaedge.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Katrina Zhou <katrina@novaedge.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation — staggered onramp, minimum floor & fallback design

Thanks Aditya — that's exactly the clarity we needed. 

Katrina and I reviewed the numbers and we are comfortable with:

- Soft floor confirmed: 8 GPUs reserved (billed) + standby buffer at reduced rate.
- Pilot activation: target start 2026-10-15, ramp to 24 GPUs by 2026-11-26 (6-week progressive activation tied to throughput triggers).
- Warm-start credits: use for two 48h A/B windows (week 2 & week 4) to validate quantized fallback variant.

Next steps for Redwood: please send an updated worksheet with explicit billing rows and a short appendix describing the queue-to-gpu math (we can include that in our internal procurement packet). Once we have that we can issue a PO.

Appreciate you moving quickly — look forward to the worksheet.

—Jordan
Jordan Ellis
Head of Infrastructure, NovaEdge AI
j.ellis@novaedge.ai
